title: Exception Handling Middleware
description: Learn how to gracefully handle unhandled exceptions in ASP.NET Core using built-in exception handling middleware, developer exception pages, and custom error pages.

blocks.text: Unhandled exceptions are inevitable in any application. A database connection might fail, a file could be missing, or a user might submit unexpected data. Without proper exception handling, these errors result in raw stack traces being returned to the client — exposing sensitive information and providing a poor user experience.

ASP.NET Core provides two primary built-in approaches for handling exceptions: the Developer Exception Page for local development, and the Exception Handler Middleware for production environments. Using the right approach in each environment keeps your application secure and your users informed.

blocks.title: Warning: Never expose stack traces in production
blocks.text: The Developer Exception Page shows sensitive information like connection strings, file paths, and source code. It must never be enabled in production. Always use UseExceptionHandler for production environments.

During development, ASP.NET Core automatically enables the Developer Exception Page when the environment is set to Development. This page provides detailed error information including the stack trace, query strings, headers, and route data — invaluable for debugging.
The Developer Exception Page is enabled by default in the CreateBuilder template. If you need to enable it manually, call app.UseDeveloperExceptionPage() in your pipeline configuration.

blocks.title: Developer exception page in development
blocks.content: Manually enabling the developer exception page for debugging during local development.

blocks.text: The if/else pattern ensures developers get full debugging information locally, while production users see a clean error page. The UseHsts() call in the else block adds HTTP Strict Transport Security headers, another production-only security measure.

The Exception Handler Middleware (app.UseExceptionHandler) catches unhandled exceptions and redirects the request to a specific path. This path should map to an error handling endpoint that renders a user-friendly error page and logs the exception details.

Unlike the Developer Exception Page, the Exception Handler Middleware does not expose error details to the client. It is the correct choice for any non-development environment. The error handling endpoint receives the original exception through the IExceptionHandlerFeature service.

blocks.title: Custom error handling with Exception Handler Middleware
blocks.content: Configure exception handling and an error controller action that logs and displays a friendly error page.

blocks.text: In the Error action, IExceptionHandlerFeature provides access to the original exception. You can use this to log the full details for debugging while showing only a generic message to the user. Never pass the exception object or its message directly to the view in production.

The Status Code Pages Middleware (app.UseStatusCodePages) handles HTTP error status codes like 404 Not Found and 500 Internal Server Error. It is separate from exception handling because a 404 is not always caused by an exception — it is simply a response status.
You can configure status code pages to return plain text, JSON, or redirect to a dedicated error page for each status code range.

blocks.title: Configuring status code pages
blocks.content: Different ways to handle HTTP error status codes with the Status Code Pages Middleware.

blocks.title: Tip: Re-execute preserves the original URL
blocks.text: UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute re-runs the request through the pipeline on a different path while keeping the original URL in the browser. This lets your error page access the original route data via RouteData. Use this when you need the original URL for logging or display.
Global Exception Handling with a Filter

For MVC and API controllers, you can use an Exception Filter as an alternative to middleware-based error handling. Exception filters run after the middleware pipeline and can catch exceptions within specific controllers or actions.

blocks.title: Global exception filter for MVC controllers
blocks.content: An exception filter attribute that catches exceptions and returns a standardized JSON response for API controllers.

blocks.text: Exception filters are useful when you want different error handling behavior for different parts of your application. For example, you might return JSON for API controllers and HTML views for MVC controllers. The filter approach gives you that granularity.

terms.definition: A detailed error page shown during development with stack traces and request data. Never enable in production.
Middleware that catches unhandled exceptions and redirects to a configured error path. Used in production.
A service that provides access to the original exception details inside the error handling endpoint.
Middleware that handles HTTP error status codes like 404 and 500 with custom responses.
An MVC filter that catches exceptions within controllers, providing an alternative to middleware-based error handling.

blocks.title: Implement Production-Grade Error Handling
blocks.description: Add robust exception handling and status code pages to an existing ASP.NET Core project.
steps: Create a new MVC project: 'dotnet new mvc -n ErrorHandlingDemo'
Create an ErrorViewModel class in the Models folder with Message and RequestId properties
Create an Error action in HomeController that reads IExceptionHandlerFeature, logs the exception, and returns the Error view
Create an Error.cshtml view that displays the Message and shows RequestId if available
In Program.cs, add UseDeveloperExceptionPage for Development and UseExceptionHandler('/Home/Error') with UseHsts for other environments
Add app.UseStatusCodePagesWithReExecute('/Home/Error') to handle 404 and other status codes
Run the app, navigate to a non-existent route to see the error page, and verify no stack trace is exposed
blocks.expectedOutcome: Visiting a non-existent route shows a clean error page without stack traces. In Development mode, the developer exception page shows full details. All errors are logged through ILogger for later review.

items.text: I can configure conditional exception handling based on IHostEnvironment
items.hint: Use IsDevelopment() to choose between the two approaches.

items.hint: HSTS requires a valid HTTPS certificate and should not be enforced during local development.

I can configure Status Code Pages to handle 404 and 500 errors

items.text: I know when to use an exception filter instead of middleware
items.hint: Use filters when you need different error handling per controller or action.

blocks.title: Exception Handling Summary
points: Always use the Developer Exception Page only in Development environment
UseExceptionHandler with a dedicated error path is the production approach
IExceptionHandlerFeature provides access to the original exception inside error endpoints
Status Code Pages Middleware handles non-exception HTTP errors like 404 Not Found
Exception filters provide controller-level error handling as an alternative to middleware
Never pass raw exception messages or stack traces to the browser in production
blocks.takeaway: Proper exception handling protects your users from confusing error pages and protects your application from leaking sensitive information. Combining middleware-based handling with exception filters gives you complete coverage from the pipeline down to individual controllers.
